numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Under Numba on Python 3.14+, multiplying a complex infinity by a real scalar returns (inf+nanj) instead of CPython's (inf+2j). The same wrong result appears for the reversed operand order, mul(2.0, z).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The jitted result should match plain CPython 3.14 semantics: z*2.0 with z=complex(inf,1.0) should give (inf+2j), and 2.0*z should also give (inf+2j).
trigger_conditions: complex operand with an infinite component (z=complex(float('inf'), 1.0))
multiplication of that complex value by a real float scalar (2.0), in either operand order
Numba still promotes the real to complex(x, 0j) and uses the full complex kernel instead of CPython's mixed-mode path

input_output_examples.input: def mul(z, x): return z * x; z=complex(float('inf'), 1.0); mul(z, 2.0)
def mul(z, x): return z * x; z=complex(float('inf'), 1.0); mul(2.0, z)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: large finite value 1e200 used so multiplication can overflow before recovery; 1e200 is a special-value input in TestComplexNaNRecovery
category_specific_evidence: Special values in TestComplexNaNRecovery: -0.0, +0.0, 1, -1, 1e200, +inf, -inf, nan, combined by itertools.product over real and imaginary parts
NaN recovery for complex mul/div added for Python 3.14+ via utils.PYVERSION >= (3, 14) gate in numba/cpython/numbers.py

Recovery logic: when result is nan+nanj and a or b is infinite, sign-preserving copysign sets the infinite component to +/-1.0 and NaN components of the zero-like parts to copysign(0.0, ...), then recomputes
Same recovery applied when c or d is infinite (w infinite), with NaN parts of a,b set to signed zeros
Recovery also applies when ac, bd, ad or bc overflow to infinity and no recalc was triggered

Division: CPython division depends on FMA; numba result for z=complex(1e200,-1) divided by w=complex(1e200,-1) gave (1+0j) while CPython gave (1-4.816661538840688e-217j) on M1 mac; not reproduced on linux-aarch64 docker

NaN sign bit: complex division with z=complex(-inf, QNAN_NEG) and w=complex(-0.0,-inf) gave real NaN payload 0xfff8000000000010 in numba versus 0x7ff8000000000000 in CPython; the reporter argues CPython fails to propagate NaN payload
Mixed-mode real/complex arithmetic (issue #10780): numba promotes real to complex(x,0j), so 2.0*complex(inf,1.0) gives (inf+nanj) instead of (inf+2j); signed zeros in 2 - 0j also diverge
Tests were previously skipped on Python 3.14 (issue #10257); tests now gated by skip_unless_py314_or_later
reproduction_risks: Results depend on Python version (3.14+ only) and on FMA availability/platform (M1 mac vs linux-aarch64)
NaN sign and payload propagation differs between numba and CPython for complex division
Mixed real/complex operations (issue #10780) are not covered by the complex kernel fix and remain divergent
Test values include large finite 1e200 to trigger overflow; results sensitive to exact input values
